sections.h2: Where is Hancock County, Iowa, and what towns does it include?
sections.html:
Hancock County is in north-central Iowa, bordered by Winnebago County to the north, Cerro Gordo to the east, Wright to the south and Kossuth to the west. Garner is the county seat. The county covers about 573 square miles and had 10,795 residents in the 2020 census.

The population peaked at 15,402 in 1940 and has slid since 1980, when it was 13,833. In 2020 the median age was 45.4, and 24.1 percent of residents were 65 or older. All residents counted were rural by census definition.

Forest City straddles the county line, which matters for taxes. A parcel is billed by the county where it sits, so a Forest City house on the Winnebago side is handled by a different treasurer.

sections.h2: How did Hancock County and Garner get started?
sections.html:
Hancock County was founded on January 15, 1851 and named for John Hancock of the Continental Congress. An election on June 28, 1858 established it fully, and the county seat moved to Garner from Concord, about a mile south, when the courthouse cornerstone was laid on June 8, 1899.

Garner was platted by the Chicago, Milwaukee and St. Paul Railroad in 1870 and incorporated on November 19, 1881. It was named for a railroad engineer, Col. W. W. Garner. Fred and August Duesenberg ran a bicycle shop in town in the 1880s before building the Duesenberg car, and Garner marks that each year with Duesey Days.

Forest City was once called Puckerbrush. It was officially founded in 1855, platted in 1856 and incorporated June 14, 1878, after local leaders persuaded the Minneapolis and St. Louis Railroad to route through it. Swedish and Norwegian settlers came to a landscape that looked like home.

sections.h2: What jobs and employers shape the Hancock County housing market?
sections.html:
Manufacturing and education are the named employers in the county's two largest towns. Forest City is where Winnebago Industries, the motorhome maker, began in 1960 when investors took over a failing travel trailer factory. The company announced in August 2021 that it would move its corporate headquarters to Eden Prairie, Minnesota, but keep manufacturing in Forest City.

Waldorf University, a private four-year school, is also in Forest City, and the Forest City Community School District runs a wind turbine that supplies about 60 percent of its schools' energy needs.

In Garner, Stellar Industries and Iowa Mold Tooling Company make truck-mounted equipment such as service cranes and mechanics trucks. The county's school districts include Garner-Hayfield-Ventura (formed July 1, 2015), Forest City, West Hancock, Belmond-Klemme and West Fork, along with Algona and Clarion-Goldfield-Dows.

A county with a falling and aging population has a steady supply of older houses coming up for sale. Owners of those houses often find that repairs and unpaid taxes both need attention before a conventional listing works.

sections.h2: What does the north-central Iowa climate mean for a Hancock County house?
sections.html:
Winters in Hancock County are hard on roofs, furnaces and pipes. Forest City's climate is classed as hot-summer humid continental, with about 35.92 inches of precipitation and 40.2 inches of snow in an average year. Recorded extremes there run from 108 degrees Fahrenheit in July to minus 36 in winter.

For a seller, that range explains the usual inspection list on older rural and small-town houses: roof condition, insulation, heating equipment and basement moisture. Buyers who finance often need these items fixed or priced in. An as-is cash buyer can skip the repair step, though any lien, back tax or open permit still has to be cleared at closing.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Hancock County?
sections.html:
The Hancock County Treasurer collects property tax at the Courthouse, 855 State Street, Garner, IA 50438, Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., closed holidays. The assessor's office handles valuations and exemptions.

  • First half: due September 1, delinquent October 1.
  • Second half: due March 1, delinquent April 1.
  • You can also pay the full year in September.
  • Delinquent owners get a notice on November 1 and May 1.
  • Paying in person by debit card adds $2.00; a credit card adds 2.25 percent. Online, an eCheck costs $0.25 and cards carry the same fees.

The county treasurer's phone is 641-923-3122. The county's page also lists elderly and disabled credits, but it notes figures that appear to be from 2023, so confirm current limits with the office before relying on them. The 65-plus homestead exemption requires a new application through the assessor even if a credit is already on file.

sections.h2: How do Hancock County assessment appeals work?
sections.html:
A Hancock County owner who disagrees with a valuation files a written protest with the Board of Review between April 2 and April 30. The Hancock board has five members and meets on or about May 1.

The protest has to name one of the grounds in Iowa Code 441.37: the value is inequitable compared with similar property, it exceeds what the law allows, the property is misclassified or exempt, there is an error, or there was fraud. The board must send a written decision with its reasons.

Iowa residential rollback is a state number, set each year to keep taxable growth to 3 percent across the state. A 2025 example from the Iowa Taxpayers Research foundation used a residential rollback of 44.5345 percent. Rollback does not cap local levy rates, so a bill can still rise.

Iowa is also replacing the homestead credit with a homestead exemption of 10 percent of taxable value, with a minimum of $5,500 and a maximum of $20,000, starting with assessment year 2026.

sections.h2: How does the Hancock County tax sale work?
sections.html:
Hancock County holds its annual tax sale online on the third Monday of June, starting at 9:00 a.m., and bidders register through iowataxauction.com. The treasurer must offer parcels with delinquent taxes under Iowa Code chapter 446.

  • The official parcel list appears around June 1 and is updated daily until the sale.
  • Delinquent taxes are advertised in an official county newspaper in June, although the publication fee is charged on May 1 regardless.
  • The county's tax sale page gives a payment deadline of May 20, 2025 to avoid publication. That date is from an earlier year, so ask the treasurer for the current cutoff.
  • Notice of the sale must be mailed by May 1 to the name the parcel is taxed under.
  • Redeeming a parcel needs guaranteed funds and carries 2 percent interest per month.

An owner who has fallen behind on a Hancock County house should not wait for the June list. Selling before the sale lets the taxes be paid from proceeds rather than redeemed at 2 percent a month.

sections.h2: What happens to property tax when you sell in Hancock County?
sections.html:
Taxes are prorated at closing or paid by the seller to the treasurer directly, and they always run a year behind. A sale between July 1 and December 31 leaves the seller owing the September installment, while a sale from January 1 to June 30 leaves the March one.

Iowa's state transfer tax is 80 cents for each $500 of value above $500 (Iowa Code 428A.1). A declaration of value is submitted to the county recorder with the deed. The recorder forwards it to the assessor, who keeps it for three years from December 31 of the transfer year.

Late interest is 1.5 percent per month and begins the first day after the installment goes delinquent. A missing statement does not waive it, since the state says the owner is responsible for making sure a bill is received.

faqs.q: When are Hancock County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and goes delinquent October 1. The second half is due March 1 and goes delinquent April 1. You can also pay the full year in September.

faqs.q: Where is the Hancock County Treasurer?
faqs.a: The office is at the Courthouse, 855 State Street, Garner, Iowa 50438. Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday to Friday, and the phone is 641-923-3122.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to redeem a Hancock County tax sale parcel?
faqs.a: Redemption needs guaranteed funds and carries 2 percent interest per month on top of the amount the parcel sold for. Ask the treasurer for an exact payoff.

faqs.q: Is Forest City in Hancock County?
faqs.a: Partly. Forest City lies in both Hancock and Winnebago counties, so the county where the parcel sits determines which treasurer bills the tax.
